column1: # Module/configuration pairs that legitimately resolve a dependency to something other than the
# version a bump declares. Read by run-bump-gate.sh step 0.
# Step 0 asserts that a bump actually took effect, by checking the RESOLVED version rather than the
# declared one. Its original rule was "exactly one version across the whole repository", and that
# rule is wrong for a repo which builds libraries AND independent APKs: an application module with
# its own APK never shares a runtime classpath with the library modules, so it resolving something
# different is a fact rather than a fault.
# The cost of the old rule was not a false alarm — it was worse. Two bumps in a row (media 1.8.0,
# and appcompat 1.8.0 before this file) could not be gated with a coordinate at all, so step 0 was
# SKIPPED and the check that distinguishes "safe" from "had no effect" simply did not run. A check
# too blunt to be used is not a strict check; it is an absent one.
# "This exact module/configuration resolves this exact version, for this recorded reason, and that
# is expected." It is NOT a waiver on the coordinate as a whole: every OTHER row still has to be the
# expected version, so a new non-uniformity in a different module still fails.
# TWO RULES THAT KEEP THIS FROM BECOMING A MASK
#   1. An entry that matches NOTHING in the run is a FAILURE, not a pass. An allowlist entry
#      outliving the condition it waives is a silent hole — the same lesson the PreferenceTest
#      intermittent entry taught when its defect was fixed at source and the waiver was deleted
#   2. Every entry needs a reason, and the reason has to say why the difference is harmless rather

column5: Transitive via androidx.car.app:app:1.7.0. Host A is an APPLICATION module with its own APK, so it never shares a runtime classpath with car-media-common; forcing uniformity would change what Host A loads for no benefit. androidx.media is deprecated in favour of Media3, so the long-term fix is a migration rather than a pin.

Transitive via androidx.constraintlayout:constraintlayout. car-rotary-lib declares no appcompat and compiles against none, so nothing in it raises what constraintlayout drags in; its own instrumented tests run on debugAndroidTestRuntimeClasspath, which resolves the expected version. Adding a declaration to force uniformity would mean declaring a dependency the module does not use. Verified pre-existing by stashing the bump and re-measuring, and unchanged by constraintlayout 2.2.2.
Transitive via constraintlayout -> appcompat 1.2.0, the path the appcompat row records. car-rotary-lib declares and imports no fragment; its instrumented tests resolve 1.8.9 through :car-ui-lib.
